design:
# Machine signing and NixOS dogfooding preparation

Date: 2026-09-13. Status: draft for operator discussion, not an implementation or deployment instruction. No keys were generated or decrypted, no product source/configuration changed, and no builds or VM lifecycle operations ran. Planning artifacts and native tracker notes are the only intended local writes.

## Decision to make first

Provide a small integrated operator workflow that creates a machine SSH signing key, encrypts its private material using an explicitly selected fleet's existing SOPS/age policy, and returns its copyable public key and fingerprint. The installed CLI does not currently provide this workflow. Reuse existing secret-target resolution and cryptographic primitives; do not confuse age wrapping-key generation with SSH identity generation.

Recommended first scope:

- Ed25519 signing-only key, stored under one named fleet secret domain with the existing SOPS recipients. Preserve recipients, other secret values and existing keys.
- SOPS encryption at rest with unattended authorized use. An additional OpenSSH passphrase would need a new unlock design: the current sealed-key parser rejects it.
- Public output only. Refuse overwrite, ambiguous targets, partial encryption and unintended cross-fleet writes. Preserve multiline OpenSSH key bytes through encryption and native parsing.
- Manual registration of the public key as a **signing key on the machine GitHub account**. The current operator shell authenticates as `georgrybski`; an unqualified GitHub key-upload command there would target the wrong account.
- No automatic change to machine HTTPS tokens, human author metadata, SSH login grants, host Git configuration, host agent, workload configuration or deployment.

The command spelling remains a proposal. The [signing assessment](../assessment-reports/2026-09-13-machine-signing-key-assessment.md) separates actual help output, existing primitives and suggested interface names. Do not run hypothetical commands as if they existed.

Questions for the operator: confirm SOPS-only unattended encryption versus a separate passphrase-unlock requirement; decide one shared machine key versus separately revocable keys per fleet. Recommended default is one explicitly selected fleet first, with separate keys for another fleet while keeping the same machine GitHub identity if desired.

## Signing integration is a separate acceptance step

Generation and encrypted storage can be implemented independently of complete SSH broker repair. Making ordinary guest `git commit` use the key requires its own real runtime path and fleet Git configuration. Current library signing authorization is not proof of a working guest adapter.

Keep signing catalog entries, `git` namespace and per-workload grants distinct from SSH connection authentication. Preserve broker-only private-key custody. Before enabling real signing material, verify that it is absent from guest bootstrap, process arguments, logs and the Nix store. Validate a real signed commit, machine committer identity, GitHub verification, restart identity, wrong namespace, missing grant and cross-fleet denial. GitHub authentication alone does not prove signing or repository contribution rights.

GitHub documents [SSH signing configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/telling-git-about-your-signing-key) and [separate signing/authentication registration](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/adding-a-new-ssh-key-to-your-github-account). No account registration was performed here.

## Persistence and fresh installation are not yet one green gate

Fresh GitHub metadata in this assessment:

| Component | Remote default / status | Local or installed distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workestrate | `main` at `96f2ed1`; [PR36](https://github.com/rybskiworks/workestrate/pull/36) at `a173604`, open and blocked | Installed package is `d0xzq57...`, baked source `082c526`; primary checkout is `f9ffa91`. Cached tracking refs do not establish current remote equality. |
| nix-tooling | `main` at `a403c2c`, no open PR | Local checkout matches. Consumer locks still require their own exact-version assessment. |
| Personal fleet | `main` at `6308438`; current features in open PR23–30, plus old draft22 | Local deployment source `e9b36c8` has additional dirty changes; a fresh default-branch clone is not the deployed fleet. |
| Tool-home configuration | `main` at `3110361`; open PR2 then PR3 | Local `memory-publication-jobs` is `6d8000a` plus dirty configuration. |
| Duelbits fleet | `main` at `406517e`; open PR1 at `cce3110` | Local checkout is the feature commit. |

These refs were read without fetching, merging, pulling or changing the installed profile. Remaining integration is tracked separately from present runtime usability; do not tell a clean NixOS host to install arbitrary default refs and expect the accepted runtime.

All three memory repositories are private and have persisted `main` branches:

- [CTF](https://github.com/rybskiworks/ai-memory-ctf): `3dbaea54ae2f257a62db9adba885c9d7cb6d93d0`, the verified final185-commit wiki publication.
- [Personal](https://github.com/rybskiworks/ai-memory-georgrybski): `913dc749aef10a69882a6e0643c07340c71b4d4c` at this observation.

Wiki Git history is not a raw SQLite/session backup. Full raw-memory off-host recovery remains open. Native Beads has a recent full **local** Dolt backup at `assessment-reports/private-state/2026-09-08-beads.fc2KtI/post-adoption.dolt`; the current configured source remote is public and is not an approved private tracker destination. The old legacy backup-status timestamp is distinct from the successful native Dolt backup sync.

Fresh host service metadata also confirms personal and Duelbits wiki publishers succeeded at15:30:11Z and15:30:26Z with active timers. This does not prove pre-login operation on another NixOS host: the current publisher uses the authorized operator's host GitHub authentication. The [personal fleet assessment](../assessment-reports/2026-09-13-personal-fleet-dogfooding-readiness.md) records exact mounts, package selections, command semantics and remaining gaps. In particular, the selected LiteLLM image is still its registry1.98 image rather than the shared NixOS parent, and shared Dolt is not deployed or connected to Prime. Do not claim uniform-base or shared-tracker completion.

## Two separate dogfooding tests

1. **Resident Prime development:** use the existing normal Prime behavior and normal project/config discovery. Start with a named disposable project and preflight; confirm effective workload/image/runtime identity, `/dev/kvm`, guest-owned Determinate daemon/store, XDG/state roots, disk/RAM budget and machine Git identity without printing credentials. Ordinary Prime/provider/memory use has prior evidence; inner Workestrate lifecycle is not proved by that evidence.
2. **Fresh NixOS installation:** install a reviewed exact Workestrate package ref with the NixOS host prerequisites declared explicitly. Workestrate exports a Nix package/app, not a ready NixOS service module. Test an independent clean NixOS guest as the packaging/control baseline; separately test the Microsandbox-hosted Prime environment. Success in one backend is not success in the other.

After preflight, progress through clone → edit → pinned devenv → a uniquely uncached sandboxed guest build → build inner image → inner create/wait/exec/inspect/stop → persistence/restart. Use an independent inner Workestrate home **and backend runtime/state roots**; `--home` alone is not proof of complete isolation. Do not mount the host Nix daemon socket or writable host store into the lab.

Prior foundation evidence is stronger than merely a NixOS/QEMU control: `/tmp/ns.T64ZnB/ng.73c5_4hp/result.json` records full direct-Microsandbox acceptance for an older exact runtime/base/firmware pair, including sandbox builds, daemon restart, two boots with persisted data/roots and normal stop. Preserve that result, but do not substitute it for the current `fr7/251` runtime plus selected Prime leaf and inner Workestrate acceptance. Current host read-only checks show AMD nesting enabled and usable `/dev/kvm` access through an explicit user ACL; guest access still needs its own preflight.

Keep the coding agent unrestricted inside its VM. Do not add a special reduced-capability Prime configuration. Apply resource/lifecycle containment at the VM boundary, with separate untrusted-client fixtures to test the Nix sandbox. Preserve shared memory/LiteLLM services and existing host toolchains. Nested negative-policy/mount tests follow the first working loop rather than being represented as already accepted.

No launch command was executed in this assessment. `workload exec prime` can perform dependency and image preparation depending on current state; it is not a guaranteed no-build attachment. The actual launch sequence should be selected after preflight and the requested signing-spec discussion.

title: Preserve ai-memory session identity through health wrappers and LiteLLM transport
description: Owner: rybskiworks/ai-memory on the existing upstream-contribution branch. Source assessment of selected 0b5edf3ed1ce56c81b6e51d4665f56efb866009d confirms that consolidation supplies session-derived LlmOperationId, but serve wraps the provider in HealthRecordingLlmProvider whose legacy-only methods discard it. Generic openai-compat also has no dynamic gateway identity; native opencode sends a final header which the fleet gateway intentionally reserves. Implement narrow forwarding and opt-in validated gateway operation-header support using existing abstractions; do not disable admission, invent static session IDs, or move application logic into Workestrate. Planning evidence: assessment-reports/2026-09-12-ai-memory-litellm-integration.md. No source tests/builds/deployments are authorized in the current planning-only turn.
acceptance_criteria: Forward plain and structured operation-aware calls through health recording and fallback while preserving exactly-once result accounting. Real session identity survives repeat calls, structured fallback, durable-job retry/restart and wrapper composition. Opt-in generic x-litellm-session-id support preserves standalone logical-operation identity without claiming unrelated operations are one agent conversation; reject invalid/conflicting configured headers and keep final x-opencode-session gateway-owned. Unit/mock tests cover all completion methods, distinct sessions, candidate failures and unchanged health snapshots; extend actual-service/LiteLLM fixture under wrk-lcj.7.8, not only a direct provider object. Document configuration and limitations. Keep feature branch intended for upstream; do not merge it into fork main merely to publish this repair.

description: Read-only host checks on 2026-09-12 found personal LiteLLM run27/PID714922 still Running and port4000 listening, but two GET /health/liveliness requests ended RemoteDisconnected before HTTP. title: Bind conversation affinity to host-bound credential material versions
description: The live LiteLLM gateway uses host-bound OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY bindings. Workestrate and Microsandbox expose stable MSB placeholders inside the guest; actual credentials are substituted later by the host egress proxy. The callback therefore derives a slot-scoped UUID, not an actual-secret-scoped UUID. Same-slot key rotation leaves UUID unchanged and identical keys under different slots produce different UUIDs. Synthetic literal-key tests do not prove production rotation behavior. Preserve existing host custody; do not silently switch provider keys to guest-bound.

title: Compose isolated builder and read-only cache fleet workloads
description: Personal fleet owns service capsules, workload flakes and actual MSB tests; reuse the nix-tooling base/daemon tasks rather than creating a second bootstrap. acceptance_criteria: Real guest-owned multi-user daemon and sandboxed uncached build; remote execution proven through pinned ssh-ng command, exact host keys and an isolated builder trust domain. Restricted SSH is not read-only daemon access; trusted submitters are administrator-equivalent. Two-client cache reuse; cold start/restart/cancellation/concurrency quotas, disk admission, exact child teardown, state recovery. No host daemon/home/store socket mounts, no sandbox-disable fallback, no release keys available to agents. Nested KVM is a separate opt-in gate.
notes: Actual guest readiness now requires the Determinate activation gate wrk-8pl.3.2 in addition to signed-cache contract. Preserve separate builder, consumer and private publisher trust domains; no shared writable store, signer credentials in consumers or SSH-ng read-only assumption.

acceptance_criteria: Build submission, signing, publishing and read authorization remain separate. No whole-store publication or automatic upload on entering devenv. Approved-path-only publication, atomic availability, bounded retries/status, retention/GC roots, recovery and signing-key rotation; personal/company/untrusted domains stay distinct. Client configurations include endpoint and public keys only. Actual hosted upload uses a separately approved narrowly scoped identity and explicit remote test.

Fresh destination per negative rejects unsigned input-addressed output, wrong key, tampered NAR, wrong reader auth and unavailable endpoint; no local fallback or existing valid output masks rejection. Reader cannot upload. Exercise manifest path/symlink/unknown-field rejection. Use explicit private HTTP substitution, not --offline which disables substituters.

description: Owners: Workestrate mount-policy compiler/wire and Microsandbox evaluator. compile.rs retains stable scope-instance order, but both program evaluators reconstruct write order from scope kind, deny/allow bucket and bucket index. A config layer allowing x followed by a config layer denying x therefore resolves allow instead of the required later-layer deny. Read order retains the correct result. This is source-level evidence, not a newly executed runtime regression. Non-goals: treating all denies as a union, changing terminal/protect semantics, inferring layer identity from labels, or adding an unversioned persistent wire field.
acceptance_criteria: Focused equal-kind two-layer tests cover allow-to-deny and deny-to-allow, repeated instances, terminal rules and operator protect on both axes. Independent scope-instance oracle and serialized compiler/runtime behavior agree. Choose and test old/new wire compatibility deliberately, including old policy loading and unsupported versions. Run Workestrate pinned unit/Clippy checks plus runtime offline mount_policy tests; no fleet or KVM prerequisite for the initial regression/fix.

This is a validation mismatch, not proof of host-device escape. Non-goals: mounting over sensitive paths for a demonstration, silently normalizing only one lookup layer, or changing host source provenance/state roots.
acceptance_criteria: Pure fixtures reject equivalent sensitive guest destinations before runtime creation, preserve valid harmless paths and prefix lookalikes, and consistently cover normalized duplicates, mount-entry policy lookup and policy-file slug identity. Test /probe/./child only as an optional harmless guest control. Workestrate pinned unit/Clippy checks pass; no VM or live mount is required to establish the primary regression.

This is a source-confirmed counterexample, not an executed guest leak or host escape. Non-goals: real secret mounts, masking pathnames alone, disabling policy in the primary reproducer, write/tag semantics or changes in an unconsumed historical checkout.

A nested directory/public counterpart preserves allowed descendant reachability. Cover known-inode/getattr and single-file adapters without making regular files traversable. Run pinned offline microsandbox-filesystem mount_policy tests in an xattr-capable scratch environment; then a direct isolated guest probe must pass the positive control and fail nonzero on forbidden listing/read. Publish and consume the exact corrected runtime revision before protected host mounts or real credentials; no xfail or missing-capability success.

title: Adopt the shared warm store for runner caches (builder VM, overlay generations)
description:
Today the runner machine mounts workspaces/workestrate/build-cache read-write into every instance: one shared cache, content-addressed images, FICLONE copy-on-write root disks. That is the cache plane we actually have.

The larger shape is designed but not implemented: a builder/cache microVM that owns builds, an immutable publication store, and per-VM /nix/store as shared immutable lower plus private writable upper through OverlayFS with the Lix local-overlay store, plus KSM for RAM dedup (see the tool repository's docs/shared-nix-store-fabric.md).

Memory-level fork or snapshot does not exist in the pinned backend: the same document records that true warm-template memory CoW needs VM snapshot/restore or fork semantics, a substantially larger VMM feature. Scaling today means more instances over the warm cache, not a fork of a running one.
acceptance_criteria:
- Measured cold-start and gate time for a runner instance, warm cache vs empty cache.
- A decision with evidence: keep the shared cache mount, or move to published generations.
- If a fork/snapshot requirement is real, it is written as a backend feature request with the measured queue wait that motivates it.

title: ensure-images: keep eval-error fail-closed vs nix-absent trust posture — document decision
description:
Objective: record and document the decision to KEEP the ensure-images fail-closed posture on nix eval errors, distinct from the nix-absent trust posture. This is a documentation/decision bead — no code change.

Decision (recorded 2026-08-03):
- Eval errors (nix build fails to evaluate the image drvPath) → FAIL-CLOSED: surface the eval error and refuse up/exec. Rationale: an eval error almost always conceals a real config bug (a missing attr, a broken overlay, a stale lock), so trusting past it would silently run a stale/foreign image. The operator must fix the config.
- nix-absent (the `nix` binary is unavailable, e.g. a standalone install with no nix) → TRUST posture: ensure-images degrades to trusting the msb image store and only forces a build/load when a tag is absent. This is the documented standalone-install path (spec 21 §3.4 skew matrix, §8).
- Tag-absent (nix present or absent) → ALWAYS forces a build/load; never trusted.

The two postures are deliberately different: eval-error is a CONFIG signal (fix the config), nix-absent is an ENVIRONMENT signal (no nix to evaluate with). Conflating them would either mask config bugs (if eval-error trusted) or break standalone installs (if nix-absent fail-closed). The current code keeps them separate; this bead records the rationale so a future refactor does not collapse them.

Related spec: 21-image-build-lifecycle.md §3 (change detection — the eval-only drvPath signal), §3.4 (skew matrix), §8 (state schema). Cross-ref: this decision is noted in spec 21 §15 open follow-ups.
